Their saliva contains amylase, a substance that breaks down starch. This saliva is also thickened with mucus, a slippery substance that keeps tissues moist.

tier2.text: Each submandibular gland makes saliva and sends it into the mouth through the submandibular duct, a tube through which a gland releases its contents. Each submandibular gland lies beneath the mandible, the bone of the lower jaw. The submandibular glands are one of the three pairs of major salivary glands; the other two are the parotid and sublingual glands. Each submandibular gland is a compound tubuloalveolar gland, a gland built from a combination of tubes and pockets. The gland's secretory cells include serous cells, which secrete a watery fluid containing amylase for digesting starch. The gland also has mucous cells, which secrete mucus, a thick, slippery substance that keeps tissues moist. As a result, submandibular saliva contains amylase, but in a liquid thickened with mucus. Chemicals in food stimulate taste receptors on the tongue, which signal the brain stem to send back nerve impulses that stimulate salivation. The impulses that reach each submandibular gland travel through the facial nerve.
